text: The break count and the break limit are composed, not stored. The count is the number of treatments of the same case whose outcome is BROKEN (LOV-TRT-OUTCOME) plus the break count the case signal carries, and the limit is the max_breaks value of the RESTRUCTURE rule row in force, read with its version. Both are inputs of the detectBrokenPlan activity and fields of the PlanBreak element; no break-count column, no break-count field identifier and no fixed limit is added or asserted, and the composition is the working read until the owner publishes the field or the row.
why: R-RES-29 increments a break count, R-RES-30 and R-RES-31 test it against max_breaks and R-RES-36 catches a count that is missing, and no source gives either value a column, a field identifier or a governed row.

text: The event REQ-S2-009 speaks of is the BREAK_RECORDED stage report the break branch sends to the parent CaseWorkflow as a Temporal signal inside the case. No Kafka event is published for a broken plan by these two stories: rwb.treatment.events.v1 keeps its one catalogued event EV-10 TreatmentApproved, no outbox row is written by the break step, and a Kafka event is left to the gap until the owner allocates a name, a payload and its consumers and the plan adds DP-09.
why: REQ-S2-009 says a broken plan raises an event, while the ownership rows give S2 one event only and the split plan gives both stories no event-platform dependency, so an event cannot be published without inventing a name and a dependency.

text: The break step writes the treatment mark only: outcome = BROKEN and outcome_at in rwb_treatment, with the PlanBreak element and the local decision record in the same transaction. Every case status of the rule — PLAN_BROKEN, BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION, RESTRUCTURE_BARRED and UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION — is applied by rwb-case from the stage report, which carries the outcome, the reason broken_plan, the break count, the limit and the 5 working day owner task of R-RES-30; recovery_case.plan_status and plan_status_as_of are read on the case signal only and never written here.
why: Three places can hold the plan status after the split, the ACE plan view is read only, and no source says which record the break step writes, so the boundary must be stated for both stories to be buildable and testable.

text: The payment evidence is read at the ACE batch date from recovery.v_ace_payment for the accounts of the plan and tested over the cure window the plan carries, counting the payments whose date falls inside the window; a count of zero with the window passed is R-RES-29, any count above zero is 'payment found' and the clear is left to R-RES-28. The cure period in days is read from the governed set in force, and no window length, no tolerance and no match column is asserted as a value.
why: R-RES-29 decides on 'no payment and cure_period passed' and R-RES-27 names cure_period_days from reference data, and no source publishes the columns, the window or the set identifier.
